correctness.rationale: For a standard Gaussian in the intrinsic (n-1)-dimensional hyperplane, separating its independent chi radius and sphere direction gives exact mean width and a 1/(n-1) factor for quadratic moments. The bivariate absolute-normal identity gives cross-edge moments 4/pi when disjoint, 4/pi+delta when distinct incident, and 2 for coincident. The cross-edge incidence count is s=sum_v deg_T(v)deg_S(v), with coincident edges counted twice therein, yielding the coefficient lambda=2-4/pi-2delta. Writing a_v=deg_T(v)-1, b_v=deg_S(v)-1 gives s=3n-4+sum_v a_v b_v. Since delta,lambda>0, the exact global optimum requires and suffices for disjoint nonleaf supports and zero common edges. Explicit 4-vertex seed and two distinct fixed attachment vertices attain it at every n>=4. Chi gamma-ratio asymptotics give limiting covariance 3delta-2/pi<0; r_3^2=8/pi gives the exact four-vertex minimum. Independent exact enumeration all 1,695,497 ordered tree pairs up to order six, 160 direct support checks, and two seeded sphere simulations corroborate the proof without substituting for it.

originality.rationale: The exact individual graphical-zonotope width-pair angular kernel and one-tree variance extremizers occur in the closest published mathematical record and are explicitly acknowledged as prior. The new mathematical conclusion is a sharp joint minimization over TWO labelled spanning-tree embeddings, whose equality requires both edge disjointness and vertex-disjoint branching support; an explicit construction realizes both conditions in every order. In particular the minimum is strictly negative at order four and converges to a nonzero negative constant. Published accessible statements checked do not imply this equality classification as their stated conclusion. The risk that it follows by an unrecorded graph-variation reformulation remains.

value.rationale: This is a natural coupled geometric extremum: two tree graphical zonotopes are each combinatorial cubes, of the same Euclidean intrinsic volume and individual mean width, but their shared-direction widths can be negatively dependent. The theorem gives the sharp order-by-order cross-covariance infimum, all optimizers on labelled trees, constructions for all n, and a nonzero negative infinite-order limit. Existing one-body path/star extremality does not decide how two independently chosen tree structures should be aligned and which structural features must be disjoint. The exact result isolates an interpretable geometric anticorrelation rather than arbitrary finite numerical slices.
